classification.difficultyReason: Requires a general area proof by comparing and rearranging equal triangular regions.

content.prompt: Prove that the area of a parallelogram is $bh$ by a method suggested by this diagram.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9, paired figures beneath the instruction
spec.description: Parallelogram ABCD and its rectangular scaffold AFED on the left; corresponding rectangle AFED on the right, connected by a rightward arrow. Retains labels, single and double parallel arrows, red dashed completion lines and both pairs of right-angle marks. Ordinary source blue strokes become black.
spec.mathematics: AD=b; ED=AF=h. F, B, E and C are collinear. AB is parallel to DC, and AD is parallel to BC. Triangles FBA and ECD have equal areas, allowing the parallelogram to be rearranged into rectangle AFED.
spec.answerVisibility: All figures and labels are permanent question givens; no proof or answer is shown.

answer.short: Triangles $FBA$ and $ECD$ have equal areas. Replacing $ECD$ with $FBA$ gives rectangle $AFED$, so the parallelogram has area $bh$.
answer.worked:
Since $BC=AD=FE$ and $BE$ is common, $FB=EC$. Also, $AF=ED=h$, so triangles $FBA$ and $ECD$ have equal bases and perpendicular heights, and therefore equal areas.

Move triangle $ECD$ to fill triangle $FBA$. This forms rectangle $AFED$ without changing the area.

$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{Area}(ABCD)&=\operatorname{Area}(AFED)\\\operatorname{Area}(ABCD)&=AD\times AF\\\operatorname{Area}(ABCD)&=bh.\end{align*}$$
